description: Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List for the search-full-text wiki move (#2253). Carries a distinctive marker — the relationship vocabulary block, including the abbreviated 'h.l.' (hijo legítimo) and 'v.o' (vecino) forms — so a test can assert the skill USED the page rather than recalling a handful of equivalents. The `keywords` and `place` fields expand nothing, so each term taken from here has to be run as its own query.

response.content:
# Spanish Genealogical Word List

## Relationship terms as they appear in parish and notarial acts

| Spanish | English | Abbreviated in the record as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hijo legítimo | legitimate son | **h.l.** |
| hija legítima | legitimate daughter | **h.l.** |
| hijo natural | son born outside marriage | h.n. |
| vecino | resident of the parish | **v.o** |
| difunto | deceased | d.to |
| abuelos paternos | paternal grandparents | ab.s pat.s |
| padrinos | godparents | pad.s |

The abbreviated forms in the right-hand column are what the clerk actually wrote, and the transcription preserves them. A search for the expanded phrase will not match an act that carries only the contraction, so run both.

## Given-name equivalents

| Spanish | Latin | English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Diego, Santiago | Iacobus | James |
| Catalina | Catharina | Catherine |
| Guillermo | Guillelmus | William |
| Juan | Joannes | John |
| Francisco | Franciscus | Francis |

Latin forms predominate in pre-19th-century parish registers even where the vernacular is Spanish, so the Latin column is the one to search for baptisms of that era.
